title: Earnings Shock: $FTNT −25%, $NOW −16%, $GOOG Alphabet Shares Fall Nearly -10%!
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
October 28, 2026 | After-Hours Market  
Wall Street is sending a clear message: Good earnings aren't always good enough.  
  
FTNT −25.41% | Fortinet  
  
Revenue increased 20% YoY to $2.08B, and GAAP EPS reached $0.86.  
Despite raising guidance and expanding its share buyback authorization, shares plunged.  
  
Narrative: Strong reported growth doesn't guarantee a positive reaction when expectations are already high.  
  
NOW −15.77% | ServiceNow  
  
Shares dropped sharply following quarterly results described as mixed.  
  
Narrative: Enterprise software valuations can be particularly sensitive to growth expectations and forward guidance.

  
GOOGL −9.87% | 

GOOG −9.62% | Alphabet  
  
Alphabet's share classes experienced substantial after-hours selling.  
  
Narrative: Investors are closely watching AI infrastructure spending, cloud growth, and the profitability of major technology platforms. The dashboard does not establish the precise cause of this decline.  


AMRZ −5.85% | Amrize

  
Revenue of $3.77B missed the $3.85B consensus, despite adjusted EPS of $1.05 beating expectations.  
Narrative: Cost inflation and interest-rate pressure remain important considerations.  
  
 TYL − 5.80% | Tyler Technologies  
  
EPS beat expectations, but revenue missed estimates. SaaS revenue grew 21.2%.  
  
Narrative: Even healthy recurring-revenue growth may not offset disappointing headline results.  
 

MRAM −5.66% | Everspin Technologies  
  
Revenue increased to $20.6M, but the company reported a GAAP loss of $0.29 per share, affected by litigation and regulatory expenses.  
  
Narrative: Revenue growth alone cannot eliminate concerns about profitability.  


PANW −6.85% | Palo Alto Networks

  
Shares declined amid cybersecurity vulnerability and patching developments rather than a confirmed earnings catalyst.

comments.body: Fortinet raised guidance, added to the buyback and still dropped 25%, so the beat was priced in weeks ago. Google at least had a search slowdown to blame, Fortinet didn't even give people that.
